prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1114; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was stopped at the signal eastbound on the main road in Pasadena, Texas, when the rear of the vehicle was struck by Driver 2, whose vehicle was traveling at a speed consistent with a sudden impact. Driver 1 reported pain in the neck and was assisted by responding medics on scene. The force of the collision appears consistent with the reported injury, and the damage to the rear bumper, trunk and taillight assembly matches the described impact. Photographs taken at the scene confirm the positions of both vehicles and the visible damage. No independent witnesses were located, though the involved parties and a responding officer confirmed that the Passenger was seated in the vehicle at the time. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the policy. No prior damage to the vehicle was known to either party or noted during the inspection. Driver 2 acknowledged following too closely and was issued a citation for failure to control speed.
